title: Ross Ulbricht & The Silk Road | Drugs, Bitcoin & Digital Outlaws
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。在这个节目中，你可以在提高英语水平的同时，聆听迷人的故事，了解这个世界上奇妙而有趣的事情。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today is the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on the theme of “Young American Outlaws”.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge。今天我们将开启一个新的三集微系列节目，这次的主题是“美国年轻法外之徒”。

sentences.en: In this series, we’ll explore the lives of young Americans whose crimes–or perhaps simply actions–have become deeply politicised.
sentences.zh: 在这个系列中，我们将探索几位美国年轻人的生活，他们的罪行——或者也许仅仅是他们的行为——已经被高度政治化了。

sentences.en: First up, in today’s episode, we’ll talk about Ross Ulbricht, the founder of the world’s biggest drug marketplace, The Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 首先，在今天的节目中，我们将聊聊 Ross Ulbricht，他是全球最大的毒品交易市场 The Silk Road 的创始人。

sentences.en: Next up, we’ll talk about Aaron Swartz, the teen prodigy and internet freedom activist who got on the wrong side of the FBI.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将聊聊 Aaron Swartz，这位少年天才和互联网自由活动家，他不幸惹恼了 FBI。

sentences.en: And then in part three, the final part, we will talk about the ongoing case of Luigi Mangione, the man accused of murdering the CEO of United Healthcare, one of the largest health insurance providers in the United States.
sentences.zh: 然后在第三部分，也就是最后一部分，我们将讨论正在审理中的 Luigi Mangione 案，他被指控谋杀了美国最大的医疗保险提供商之一联合健康集团（United Healthcare）的首席执行官。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s not waste another minute and get into the amazing story of Ross Ulbricht.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们事不宜迟，马上进入 Ross Ulbricht 的传奇故事。

sentences.en: The professional network LinkedIn is not typically a place for provocative political statements.
sentences.zh: 职场社交平台 LinkedIn 通常不是发表煽动性政治言论的地方。

sentences.en: If you look at someone’s LinkedIn page, they might describe themselves as “a passionate sales leader with 10+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry”, or “operations manager with team leadership experience”, or all manner of other, corporate-style sentences.
sentences.zh: 如果你浏览某个人的 LinkedIn 页面，他们可能会把自己描述为“一位在制药行业拥有10年以上经验、充满热情的销售领袖”，或者“具有团队领导经验的运营经理”，或者其他各种企业风格的句子。

sentences.en: In the case of one man, his LinkedIn page read slightly differently.
sentences.zh: 但对一个人来说，他的 LinkedIn 页面写得有些与众不同。

sentences.en: When FBI officers stumbled across the LinkedIn page for one Ross Ulbricht, they found it to read, “I want to use economic theory as a means to abolish the use of coercion and aggression amongst mankind,” followed by.
sentences.zh: 当 FBI 探员偶然发现 Ross Ulbricht 的 LinkedIn 页面时，他们发现上面写着：“我想利用经济学理论作为消除人类之间强迫和侵略行为的手段，”紧接着是：

sentences.en: “To that end, I am creating an economic simulation to give people a first-hand experience of what it would be like to live in a world without the systemic use of force.”
sentences.zh: “为此，我正在创建一个经济模拟，让人们亲身体验生活在一个没有系统性使用武力的世界里会是什么样子。”

sentences.en: It was an important clue as to the identity of the person behind what was at the time the world’s largest illegal online marketplace for drugs, weapons, pornography, and, in fact, practically anything: The Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的线索，指向了当时全球最大的非法在线交易市场背后的操盘手身份。这个市场就是 The Silk Road，上面贩卖毒品、武器、色情制品，事实上几乎无所不包。

sentences.en: Ulbricht first had the idea for such a marketplace shortly after finishing university at Penn State.
sentences.zh: Ulbricht 在宾夕法尼亚州立大学毕业后不久，首次萌生了建立这样一个市场的想法。

sentences.en: He had always been a smart student and managed to get excellent grades without doing too much work.
sentences.zh: 他一直是个聪明的学生，不用花太多精力就能取得优异的成绩。

sentences.en: But after graduating, he found real life to be not quite as easy.
sentences.zh: 但毕业后，他发现现实生活并没有那么容易。

sentences.en: He tried day trading, buying and selling stocks, as well as starting a video game company, but neither of those ideas had worked out.
sentences.zh: 他尝试过日间交易、买卖股票，还创办过一家视频游戏公司，但这些尝试都没有成功。

sentences.en: He then set up an online second-hand bookstore with a friend, based in Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: 随后，他和朋友在德克萨斯州奥斯汀创办了一家在线二手书店。

sentences.en: They would buy second-hand books en masse, and sell them on other marketplaces.
sentences.zh: 他们会大量收购二手书，然后放到其他交易平台上出售。

sentences.en: It was a moderate success. It never made much money, but it did teach the then 26-year-old some boring but important skills: things like inventory management, pricing, customer service, and the basics of running an online business.
sentences.zh: 这算得上是小有成功。它虽然没赚到什么大钱，但确实让当时 26 岁的他学到了一些枯燥却重要的技能：比如库存管理、定价、客户服务以及运营在线业务的基本知识。

sentences.en: And it was while working on this project that Ulbricht had another idea.
sentences.zh: 正是在做这个项目的过程中，Ulbricht 产生了另一个想法。

sentences.en: It was for a marketplace that would provide complete anonymity, allowing buyers and sellers to transact anonymously, without the website or any snooping authorities being able to identify anyone involved.
sentences.zh: 那就是建立一个提供完全匿名性的交易市场，允许买家和卖家进行匿名交易，无论是网站还是任何窥探的监管机构都无法识别参与交易的任何人的身份。

sentences.en: And this wasn’t just a business idea; it was strongly aligned with Ulbricht’s political beliefs.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个商业想法，它与 Ulbricht 的政治信仰高度契合。

sentences.en: He was a libertarian and a strong admirer of the Austrian philosopher and economist Ludwig von Mises.
sentences.zh: 他是一个自由意志主义者，也是奥地利哲学家和经济学家 Ludwig von Mises 的狂热崇拜者。

sentences.en: The Austrian School of economics argues, essentially, that the most effective economic system is one based on free markets and voluntary exchange, with minimal government interference.
sentences.zh: 奥地利学派经济学实质上认为，最有效的经济体系是建立在自由市场和自愿交换基础上的体系，政府干预应降到最低。

sentences.en: It holds that individuals act rationally to pursue their goals, and that central planning or state intervention distorts prices and leads to inefficiency.
sentences.zh: 该学派认为，个人会理性地采取行动以追求自己的目标，而中央计划或国家干预会扭曲价格并导致效率低下。

sentences.en: In other words, the most efficient system is one where individuals are left to do what they want, without any state interference.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，最有效的系统就是让个人自由地做他们想做的事，不受任何国家干预。

sentences.en: Ulbricht’s idea of a website that allowed users complete anonymity fitted right in with this political philosophy.
sentences.zh: Ulbricht 想要建立一个允许用户完全匿名的网站，这一想法正好契合了这种政治哲学。

sentences.en: Now, it wasn’t, and still isn’t, particularly difficult to access the internet anonymously - there are plenty of ways of hiding your IP address and so on, so it’s fairly trivial to access a website anonymously.
sentences.zh: 在当时，乃至现在，匿名访问互联网并不是特别困难——有很多方法可以隐藏你的 IP 地址等等，所以匿名访问一个网站是相当容易的。

sentences.en: The problem was related to payments. There was no reliable way for one stranger to pay another.
sentences.zh: 问题在于支付。当时没有一种可靠的方式让两个陌生人互相付款。

sentences.en: Card transactions could be traced, as they were linked to your identity.
sentences.zh: 银行卡交易是可以被追踪的，因为它们与你的身份绑定。

sentences.en: Sending cash through the mail was inherently risky, as the recipient could claim they didn’t receive it, or the sender might claim it was sent when it never was.
sentences.zh: 通过邮寄寄送现金本身就存在风险，因为收件人可以声称自己没有收到，或者寄件人可能声称已经寄出，但实际上根本没有。

sentences.en: And saying “meet me behind this petrol station at 10 pm and I’ll hand over the cash” wasn’t exactly ideal either.
sentences.zh: 而说“今晚10点在加油站后面见，我把现金给你”也显然不是什么理想的办法。

sentences.en: Bitcoin, as you probably know, is a cryptocurrency that can be sent digitally from one address to another without either party’s true identity being revealed.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道，比特币是一种加密货币，可以以数字方式从一个地址发送到另一个地址，而无需透露任何一方的真实身份。

sentences.en: It was perfect. Every transaction was public, so nobody could say, “I didn’t get it”, and it was also practically anonymous, meaning nobody–not the seller, not the buyer, not the authorities–nobody would be able to see the true identity of the individuals involved in the transaction.
sentences.zh: 这太完美了。每笔交易都是公开的，所以没人能说“我没收到”；同时它实际上又是匿名的，这意味着没有人——无论是卖家、买家还是监管机构——能够看到参与交易的个人的真实身份。

sentences.en: Ulbricht got to work building the first version of the website.
sentences.zh: Ulbricht 开始着手构建该网站的第一版。

sentences.en: He built it on the Tor network, which is essentially an encrypted layer of the internet that makes it impossible to trace individual users.
sentences.zh: 他在 Tor 网络上构建了它，这本质上是互联网的一个加密层，使得追踪单个用户变得不可能。

sentences.en: It took him several months, and he did it in complete secrecy, telling only his girlfriend at the time.
sentences.zh: 这花了他几个月的时间，而且他是在完全保密的情况下进行的，只告诉了当时的年轻女友。

sentences.en: He had a vision for this big marketplace where anyone could buy anything, but he knew he needed to start with one product.
sentences.zh: 他对这个任何人都可以买到任何东西的大型市场抱有愿景，但他知道自己需要从一种产品开始。

sentences.en: Any online marketplace has this chicken-and-egg problem: if a buyer comes to it and sees there’s nothing for sale, they’ll leave, and if there are no buyers, then no sellers will bother listing anything for sale.
sentences.zh: 任何在线市场都面临着这种“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题：如果买家来到这里发现什么都没得卖，他们就会离开；而如果没有买家，卖家也就懒得把任何东西挂上去卖。

sentences.en: So, Ulbricht started with something he knew there would be demand for: drugs, and in particular, magic mushrooms.
sentences.zh: 因此，Ulbricht 从他知道会有需求的东西开始：毒品，尤其是迷幻蘑菇。

sentences.en: He grew the first mushrooms himself, then listed them for sale on his website.
sentences.zh: 他自己种植了第一批蘑菇，然后把它们挂在自己的网站上出售。

sentences.en: Given that he was going to be selling drugs, he couldn’t exactly do advertising or market his website in any way, so he had to get creative.
sentences.zh: 鉴于他要卖的是毒品，他显然无法做广告或以任何常规方式推广他的网站，所以他必须发挥创意。

sentences.en: He posted on a bunch of internet forums related to drug use, purporting to be just a user, with posts like “has anyone used this website Silk Road?
sentences.zh: 他在许多与吸毒相关的互联网论坛上发帖，假装自己只是一个普通用户，发一些类似“有人用过 The Silk Road 这个网站吗？”的帖子。

sentences.en: Looks interesting.”. The website went live in February of 2011, and soon enough, the orders came rolling in.
sentences.zh: “看起来挺有趣的。”该网站于 2011 年 2 月上线，很快，订单就源源不断地涌来。

sentences.en: And he was fulfilling them all himself. Just like he had done with the second-hand books, he would take the order, package it up, print off the address and pop it in the post.
sentences.zh: 而且所有订单都是他自己发货的。就像他之前卖二手书一样，他会接单、打包、打印地址，然后寄信邮寄。

sentences.en: It started relatively slowly, but sure enough, sellers started listing their own products for sale: cannabis, MDMA, cocaine, heroin, as well as all sorts of prescription drugs, available without a doctor’s prescription, of course.
sentences.zh: 起步相对缓慢，但很快，卖家们开始把自己的产品挂上去卖：大麻、摇头丸、可卡因、海洛因，以及各种处方药——当然，这些都不需要医生的处方。

sentences.en: The website was structured in a very similar way to a site like eBay or Amazon.
sentences.zh: 该网站的结构与 eBay 或亚马逊等网站非常相似。

sentences.en: Sellers could upload pictures of their goods, a description of what was for sale, and the price, payable in Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 卖家可以上传商品图片、商品描述以及价格，并支持用比特币支付。

sentences.en: As for buyers, they could scroll through the website, perusing different drugs, reading reviews and ratings, before deciding which one to go for.
sentences.zh: 至于买家，他们可以浏览网站，仔细查看不同的毒品，阅读评论和评分，然后决定购买哪一种。

sentences.en: They would make their purchase, in Bitcoin of course, then a few days or weeks later, they would receive a package through the mail which would contain the drugs they had ordered.
sentences.zh: 他们会进行购买，当然是用比特币，几天或几周后，他们就会在邮件中收到一个包裹，里面装有他们订购的毒品。

sentences.en: They would take the drugs, and then, being good internet citizens, they would leave a review: “really good batch”, or “the pink ones aren’t as strong as the blue ones”, or simply, “great communication, A+ seller, will buy again!”.
sentences.zh: 他们会吸食这些毒品，然后，作为优秀的网民，他们会留下评价：“这批货真的很棒”，或者“粉色的没有蓝色的劲大”，或者干脆写道：“沟通顺畅，A+卖家，还会再买！”。

sentences.en: Now, before we get into any discussion of the morality of this, it was clearly a very good business: in the United States alone, there are 37 million active illegal drug users.
sentences.zh: 在我们讨论这件事情的道德性之前，这显然是一门非常好的生意：光是在美国，就有 3700 万活跃的非法吸毒者。

sentences.en: And the nature of drug use and drug addiction is that it is, almost by definition, a repeat purchase.
sentences.zh: 而吸毒和毒瘾的本质在于，从定义上讲，它几乎必然是重复购买。

sentences.en: Buy, use, buy, use, buy, use. The Silk Road facilitated this transaction, making ordering whatever drug you wanted as easy as clicking a few buttons on your computer.
sentences.zh: 购买、使用、再买、再用、再买、再用。The Silk Road 促进了这种交易，让订购你想要的任何毒品变得像在电脑上点击几个按钮一样简单。

sentences.en: The website took a fee, of course, which ranged from 8 to 15% of the transaction value, but for sellers, this was a small price to pay for the convenience.
sentences.zh: 当然，网站会收取手续费，额度在交易额的 8% 到 15% 之间，但对卖家来说，为了这种便利，付出这点代价是微不足道的。

sentences.en: Later that year, in 2011, the website caught the eye of an eager journalist at the now-defunct blog Gawker.
sentences.zh: 同年晚些时候，也就是 2011 年，该网站引起了现已停办的博客网站 Gawker 上一位热心记者的注意。

sentences.en: He published an article titled, “The Underground Website Where You Can Buy Any Drug Imaginable”.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一篇题为《在这个地下网站，你可以买到任何能想象到的毒品》的文章。

sentences.en: It led to a flood of interest in the site, and other journalists started writing up their own articles too.
sentences.zh: 这引发了人们对该网站的极大兴趣，其他记者也开始撰写自己的报道。

sentences.en: All this time, Ulbricht was managing the site himself, doing everything from fixing bugs to negotiating with hackers to providing customer service.
sentences.zh: 在这段时间里，Ulbricht 一直在独自管理这个网站，从修复漏洞、与黑客谈判到提供客户服务，什么都做。

sentences.en: It was consuming his life, and his long-time girlfriend decided enough was enough.
sentences.zh: 这占据了他生活的全部，他交往多年的女友决定不能再这样下去了。

sentences.en: She gave him an ultimatum: it’s me or the website.
sentences.zh: 她向他发出了最后通牒：要么选我，要么选网站。

sentences.en: Ulbricht chose the website. By this time, the Silk Road had become more than just a place to buy drugs.
sentences.zh: Ulbricht 选择了网站。到这时，The Silk Road 已经不仅仅是一个买卖毒品的地方了。

sentences.en: There was a real sense of community, of users being part of something that was bigger than a place to buy marijuana.
sentences.zh: 这里形成了一种真正的社区感，用户觉得自己参与了一件比单纯购买大麻更伟大的事情。

sentences.en: This was a true libertarian paradise, a place where people were allowed to make their own choices about what to buy and what to put into their bodies without the government poking its nose in.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的自由意志主义天堂，一个允许人们在没有政府插手干预的情况下，自己决定买什么以及把什么东西放进自己身体里的地方。

sentences.en: Ulbricht was completely happy for people to use the website to buy drugs; he had smoked a lot of pot as a teenager; that was his decision, and he felt no responsibility to stop people from buying or selling any kind of drug.
sentences.zh: Ulbricht 非常乐意人们使用这个网站来购买毒品；他十几岁时就抽过很多大麻，那是他自己的决定，他觉得自己没有责任去阻止人们买卖任何种类的毒品。

sentences.en: However, as the website got more and more popular, he started to see things for sale that he found more problematic.
sentences.zh: 然而，随着网站越来越受欢迎，他开始看到一些他认为更有问题的商品在售。

sentences.en: Guns with scratched-off serial numbers, for example, weapons that were clearly intended to be used for murder.
sentences.zh: 例如，被磨掉序列号的枪支，这些武器显然是打算用来谋杀的。

sentences.en: He justified this in the name of freedom of choice, of the free market, but then things got darker.
sentences.zh: 他以选择自由和自由市场的名义为这些行为辩护，但随后事情变得更加黑暗。

sentences.en: People started to list things like child pornography and individuals to be sold as sex slaves–things that even the most devoted of libertarians knew were a step too far.
sentences.zh: 人们开始挂出儿童色情制品以及被当作性奴隶贩卖的个人——这些事情连最虔诚的自由意志主义者也知道是越界了。

sentences.en: These listings would be removed, but it wasn’t always particularly easy to do.
sentences.zh: 这些商品列表会被下架，但这并不总是那么容易做到。

sentences.en: In these cases, sellers would typically disguise what was really for sale: there would be no direct mention of pornography, but instead normal pictures, cryptic code, codewords, so it was identifiable to a buyer who knew what they were looking for, but harder for anyone else to know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下，卖家通常会伪装真正出售的商品：不会直接提到色情，而是使用普通的图片、神秘的代码或暗号，这样懂行的买家能看懂，但其他人很难知道是怎么回事。

sentences.en: And, as you might expect, the site had garnered the attention of the authorities: the FBI, the DEA, and the IRS, who were crawling all over it.
sentences.zh: 正如你所料，该网站已经引起了官方的注意：FBI、DEA（美国缉毒局）和 IRS（美国国税局）都在对其进行严密监控。

sentences.en: The problem was that it seemed unbreakable.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，它似乎是坚不可摧的。

sentences.en: It was anonymous, you never knew who the sellers were, and even if a buyer's home address was identified, they could simply say they didn’t know anything about the package, and it must have been a mistake.
sentences.zh: 它是匿名的，你永远不知道卖家是谁，而且即使买家的家庭地址被确认了，他们也可以简单地声称自己对这个包裹一无所知，这一定是个错误。

sentences.en: Being sent drugs in the post, if there is no way of proving that you bought them, would not stand up in a court of law.
sentences.zh: 如果无法证明是你购买了邮寄过来的毒品，这在法庭上是站不住脚的。

sentences.en: But while this anonymity made prosecutions difficult, it also gave federal agents an opening.
sentences.zh: 虽然这种匿名性让起诉变得困难，但也给联邦探员提供了一个突破口。

sentences.en: They could pose as Silk Road customers, or even sellers, blending into the marketplace like anyone else.
sentences.zh: 他们可以伪装成 The Silk Road 的顾客，甚至是卖家，像其他人一样融入这个市场。

sentences.en: And in so doing, they discovered that the person pulling the strings behind it all went by the name Dread Pirate Roberts.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，他们发现幕后操纵一切的人使用的是“Dread Pirate Roberts”这个名字。

sentences.en: Now, Dread Pirate Roberts isn’t a name that came from nowhere; it comes from the novel The Princess Bride, and is the title that is passed down from one person to another.
sentences.zh: “Dread Pirate Roberts”这个名字并非凭空而来，它出自小说《公主新娘》，是一个代代相传的称号。

sentences.en: It seemed like it was a clever choice of pseudonym, meaning that if the user acting as Dread Pirate Roberts was ever caught, he or she could claim that they weren’t the person really behind it; they had merely assumed the role.
sentences.zh: 这 seem 像是一个聪明的假名选择，意味着如果扮演 Dread Pirate Roberts 的用户被捕，他或她可以声称自己并不是真正的幕后黑手，而只是继承了这个角色。

sentences.en: Dread Pirate Roberts wasn’t a person; it was a title.
sentences.zh: Dread Pirate Roberts 不是一个人，而是一个头衔。

sentences.en: And by the start of 2013, so two years into The Silk Road, there were federal agents all over the website.
sentences.zh: 到 2013 年初，也就是 The Silk Road 运营两年后，网站上已经到处都是联邦探员了。

sentences.en: Some had even gained administrative privileges and were helping with customer support, while others were simply sitting there, watching what was going on.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至获得了管理员权限，正在协助提供客户服务，而另一些人则只是坐在那里，观察着发生的一切。

sentences.en: But the true identity of Dread Pirate Roberts was still a mystery.
sentences.zh: 但 Dread Pirate Roberts 的真实身份仍然是一个谜。

sentences.en: There were a few clues: one agent went back to those first posts about the Silk Road from 2011, and saw that some had come from the username “altoid”.
sentences.zh: 当时有一些线索：一名探员回溯了 2011 年关于 The Silk Road 的第一批帖子，发现其中一些来自用户名“altoid”。

sentences.en: Further digging found posts on different forums from a user with this username, and then one in which he asked a programming question about Tor using his own name–Ross Ulbricht–before quickly changing it to “Frosty”.
sentences.zh: 进一步挖掘后，他们在不同的论坛上发现了该用户名用户的帖子，其中一个帖子里，他用自己的真名 Ross Ulbricht 询问了一个关于 Tor 的编程问题，随后迅速将其改为了“Frosty”。

sentences.en: By mid-2013, the authorities were certain that Ross Ulbricht was Dread Pirate Roberts, but they couldn’t exactly knock on his door and ask him politely if he was indeed the man behind The Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 到 2013 年年中，警方确信 Ross Ulbricht 就是 Dread Pirate Roberts，但他们显然不能直接去敲他的门，礼貌地问他是不是 The Silk Road 的幕后黑手。

sentences.en: Yes, he had made some slipups, but they knew that he took security extremely seriously.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实犯过一些失误，但他们知道他对安全问题极其重视。

sentences.en: He would have all sorts of safeguards in place so that any evidence linking him to The Silk Road would be heavily encrypted, and he would probably have “kill buttons” on his laptop to delete any evidence if he sensed that law enforcement authorities were closing in.
sentences.zh: 他会采取各种保护措施，使任何将他与 The Silk Road 联系起来的证据都经过高度加密，而且如果他察觉到执法人员正在逼近，他很可能会在笔记本电脑上设置“一键销毁”按钮来删除所有证据。

sentences.en: They knew they had to catch him in the act, with his laptop open and unlocked.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，必须在他使用笔记本电脑且电脑处于打开和解锁状态时，将他当场抓获。

sentences.en: In the authorities' favour was that he tended to work from public places, as using a public WiFi network gave him greater deniability.
sentences.zh: 对警方有利的是，他倾向于在公共场所工作，因为使用公共 WiFi 网络可以让他更容易推卸责任。

sentences.en: Although he had spent much of the time he operated the Silk Road on the road, travelling in places like Southeast Asia, they had tracked him down to San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 尽管在运营 The Silk Road 的大部分时间里，他都在旅途中，比如在东南亚等地旅行，但他们还是在旧金山追踪到了他。

sentences.en: And on 1 October 2013, they pounced. He was working on his laptop in a quiet area of a public library in a residential area of San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 2013 年 10 月 1 日，他们果断出击。当时他正在旧金山一个住宅区公共图书馆的安静区域里用笔记本电脑工作。

sentences.en: He heard people arguing behind him, almost like a fight was about to break out.
sentences.zh: 他听到身后有人在争吵，感觉就像是要打起来一样。

sentences.en: He turned around to see what was going on, and before he knew it, he had been bustled to the ground, his laptop snatched away before he had time to close the screen or press the keyboard shortcut to delete everything.
sentences.zh: 他转过身想看看发生了什么，还没等他反应过来，他就被按倒在地上，笔记本电脑也被夺走了，他根本来不及合上屏幕或按下快捷键来删除一切。

sentences.en: It had all been a setup; the arguing pair were federal agents.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一个圈套，那两个争吵的人其实是联邦探员。

sentences.en: He was arrested and charged with all manner of crimes.
sentences.zh: 他被逮捕并被指控犯有各种罪行。

sentences.en: The trial started in January of 2015, and he stood accused of all sorts of things that were more than merely running a libertarian marketplace.
sentences.zh: 审判于 2015 年 1 月开始，他面临的各种指控远远超出了仅仅运营一个自由意志主义交易市场的范畴。

sentences.en: These included money laundering, as well as ordering the contract killings of five people who had threatened Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 这些指控包括洗钱，以及雇凶杀害五个对 The Silk Road 构成威胁的人。

sentences.en: Now, I should add that these killings didn’t take place; it seemed that he'd been scammed, but the prosecution alleged that the intent was there.
sentences.zh: 在这里我应该补充一下，这些谋杀并没有实际发生，他似乎是被骗了，但检方指控他确实有此意图。

sentences.en: He had paid for people to be killed. In May of that year, May of 2015, he was formally sentenced to double life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, plus he had to pay back just under $200 million from his illicit gains.
sentences.zh: 他付了钱让人去杀人。同年 5 月，也就是 2015 年 5 月，他被正式判处双重无期徒刑且不得假释，此外他还必须退还近 2 亿美元的非法所得。

sentences.en: He was only 30 years old. Now, when this sentence was announced, it was greeted with a mixture of horror and praise.
sentences.zh: 当时他只有 30 岁。当这一判决公布时，人们的反应喜忧参半，既有震惊也有赞许。

sentences.en: To his libertarian supporters, he was a scapegoat; he had created an online, safer version of what people do in the real world, and were doing in the street outside the San Francisco library where he had been arrested.
sentences.zh: 对于支持他的自由意志主义者来说，他是一个替罪羊；他只是在网上创建了一个更安全的版本，来替代人们在现实世界中、以及在他被捕的旧金山图书馆外的街道上所做的事情。

sentences.en: He hadn’t forced anyone to buy or sell drugs, weapons, or anything.
sentences.zh: 他没有强迫任何人购买或出售毒品、武器或任何东西。

sentences.en: And as to the accusations of the contract killings, they said these had been invented by the authorities.
sentences.zh: 至于雇凶杀人的指控，他们称这些都是警方捏造出来的。

sentences.en: But to anti-drug campaigners and many politicians, this was a great victory.
sentences.zh: 但对于反毒品活动人士和许多政治家来说，这是一次伟大的胜利。

sentences.en: He had made hundreds of millions of dollars from drug addiction, violence, and by creating a website that enabled some of the most vile behaviours imaginable.
sentences.zh: 他通过毒瘾、暴力以及创建一个纵容了人类能想象到的最邪恶行为的网站，赚取了数亿美元。

sentences.en: Yes, he was guilty, yes, he knew the risks, and yes, he deserved to spend the rest of his life behind bars.
sentences.zh: 是的，他有罪；是的，他知道风险；是的，他理应在铁窗后度过余生。

sentences.en: And he would most likely have spent the rest of his life in prison had he not found an unlikely ally.
sentences.zh: 如果他没有找到一个意想不到的盟友，他很可能会在监狱里度过余生。

sentences.en: On January 21st, 2025, on his second day back in office, Donald Trump gave Ross Ulbricht a full and unconditional pardon.
sentences.zh: 2025 年 1 月 21 日，在唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫的第二天，他给予了 Ross Ulbricht 全面且无条件的赦免。

sentences.en: On the campaign trail, he had promised Libertarian voters that he would free Ulbricht, and on the day he announced it, he posted that, “the scum that worked to convict him were some of the same lunatics who were involved in the modern-day weaponisation of government against me”
sentences.zh: 在竞选期间，他曾向自由意志主义选民承诺他会释放 Ulbricht。在他宣布这一消息的当天，他发帖称：“那些致力于定他罪的败类，与参与现代政府针对我的武器化行动的疯子是同一伙人。”

sentences.en: So, today, after 11 years behind bars, Ross Ulbricht is a free man.
sentences.zh: 因此，在度过了 11 年的铁窗生涯后，今天的 Ross Ulbricht 已经重获自由。

sentences.en: His case, and the debate about his sentence, became about more than him as an individual; it became about the role of government, the individual’s right to choose, and the society we want to live in.
sentences.zh: 他的案件以及关于他判决的辩论，其意义已经超越了他个人本身；它变成了关于政府角色、个人选择权以及我们想要生活在一个怎样的社会中的讨论。

sentences.en: Where do we draw the line between personal freedom to choose and the government’s obligation to protect?
sentences.zh: 我们应该在个人选择自由与政府保护义务之间如何划定界限？

sentences.en: Should someone be punished for building the tool, or only for how others use it?
sentences.zh: 一个人应该因为制造了某种工具而受到惩罚，还是应该只因他人如何使用它而受罚？

sentences.en: Was Ulbricht sentenced for what he did, or for what he represented?
sentences.zh: Ulbricht 被判刑是因为他的所作所为，还是因为他所代表的象征意义？

sentences.en: In the end, was he a dangerous criminal, a victim of the system, or its most dangerous critic?
sentences.zh: 归根结底，他是一个危险的罪犯，是体制的受害者，还是体制最危险的批判者？

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on Ross Ulbricht and The Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 好了，关于 Ross Ulbricht 和 The Silk Road 的这一集节目到这里就结束了。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想听听你们的想法。

sentences.en: Do you think he deserved to walk free, or do you think he should still be behind bars?
sentences.zh: 你认为他应该重获自由，还是认为他应该继续留在监狱里？

sentences.en: Just head to community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away with other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 欢迎前往 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他求知欲旺盛的听众一起交流探讨。

sentences.en: And as a final quick reminder, this was part one of the mini-series on “young American outlaws”.
sentences.zh: 最后快速提醒一下，这是关于“美国年轻法外之徒”微系列节目的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up, we’ll be talking about Aaron Swartz, the boy genius and co-founder of Reddit, whose crusade for internet freedom brought him up against the FBI, and cost him his life.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将聊聊 Aaron Swartz，这位天才少年、Reddit 的联合创始人，他为互联网自由而进行的斗争使他与 FBI 产生了冲突，并最终付出了生命的代价。

sentences.en: And then in part three, we will be talking about the current case of Luigi Mangione, the young man who stands accused of murdering the CEO of one of America’s largest healthcare insurance companies.
sentences.zh: 然后在第三部分，我们将讨论目前正在审理的 Luigi Mangione 案，这位年轻人被指控谋杀了美国最大的医疗保险公司之一的首席执行官。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家安全，我们下期节目再见。
